A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with complete main text and Appendices A–I. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable comparison of the figures, tables, equations, and proofs.

before.justification: v2 reports original forecasting experiments on traffic, electricity, and solar_10_minutes in Section 5 and Appendix C, plus inference-privacy experiments in Appendix H.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments, including forecasting CRPS results in Tables 1–10 and inference-privacy results in Tables 11–13.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–6, structured subsampling, noisy gradient updates, context/forecast augmentation in Equation 1, and the inference procedure in Appendix H are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use traffic, electricity, and solar_10_minutes for the same forecasting tasks. The training-privacy, non-private utility, and inference-privacy scenarios in Appendices C and H are retained without additions or removals.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparator sets, including Seasonal and AutoETS forecasting baselines and the standard DP-SGD comparison in Appendix C.3. Corrections to malformed Seasonal names in captions do not change comparator identity or participation.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendices B, C, and H retain the same data splits, CRPS evaluation, model configurations, training budgets, privacy parameters, and testing procedures. No experimental protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The analyses of subsequence count, sampling schemes, composition, label noise, and non-private utility in Section 5 and Appendix C are unchanged. Appendix H retains the same investigation of inference-time subsampling.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five random seeds and reporting means and standard deviations in Appendix B.3. The uncertainty-reporting practices in the experimental tables and figures remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Reported numerical results, rankings, and plotted findings are unchanged throughout both PDFs. For example, Table 1 retains DeepAR traffic CRPS of 0.157 at epsilon = 0.5 and delta = 10^-7, and 0.124 without DP. Tables 5–9 change caption spelling only.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, privacy bounds, propositions, proofs, and Appendix I generalizations are unchanged. Correcting 'Datsets' in Definitions 3.5–3.6 and 'seciton' in Appendix G does not alter mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, Section 1.1, and conclusion retain the same contributions concerning structured-subsampling privacy guarantees, amplification through augmentation, and the feasibility of private forecasting. Their scientific meaning and scope are unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the privacy–utility trade-offs and the limitations in Section 4.5 and Appendices C, H, and I are retained. Qualifications about bound tightness and generalizing unequal context/forecast noise scales are unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains the same preprocessing, hyperparameters, library versions, optimization settings, and privacy-accounting details. Appendix H's implementation settings and Section 5's statement about future implementation availability are also unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix A, and the bibliography retain the same cited works and research positioning. The apparent reference changes are page and column reflow; Appendix A.2 only corrects 'exlusively' to 'exclusively'.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized spelling, hyphenation, spacing, and caption-name corrections, including 'Datsets' and 'seciton'. It also expands the funding acknowledgement to include the DAAD Konrad Zuse programme. The section structure and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 5–9 correct malformed Seasonal names in their captions, causing limited reflow and alignment changes. The longer acknowledgement shifts the impact statement and bibliography. Figures, table structures, and scientific visual content are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 adds editorial polish and a fuller funding acknowledgement, while leaving scientific evidence, reasoning, reproducibility, and organization unchanged. Seasonal was already correctly identified in v2's table rows, so the caption corrections do not resolve a substantive ambiguity. These localized edits do not establish a meaningful overall quality difference.
